one_line: A shared HTML design canvas where an agent and human edit the same brand system.
what_it_does: Leaf exposes a visual design editor's live canvas, layers, comments, and design values as WebMCP tools so an agent can build and revise brand assets alongside a person.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP is central because the agent reads and mutates structured live canvas state, including human edits and comments, with edits entering the same undoable runtime; generic UI driving would be materially less reliable.
leverage_evidence: Transcript describes the agent reading the current canvas and a human comment, warming a swatch, then reusing the exact value in a guideline.
Transcript says edits run through the same editor runtime as UI edits and are validated and undoable.
Frames show progression from canvas/editor state to coordinated brand artifacts.
execution_rationale: The video transcript and frame sheets show a coherent end-to-end brand workflow from palette exploration through guideline, poster, email header, and hero, with approval before comments; some details remain claimed rather than directly observed.
execution_evidence: 142-second video and transcript describe a multi-stage completed workflow.
Frames visibly show populated brand boards, palette swatches, typography, and assembled page designs.
Devpost screenshot confirms the submitted product and demo packaging.
impact_rationale: Designers and brand teams have a credible need for shared human-agent iteration, and the product directly addresses repeated re-explanation and loss of editable structure.
impact_evidence: Pitch targets brand foundations and downstream applications.
Transcript demonstrates carrying palette, type, and mark across deliverables without re-explaining.
Live shared canvas and comments support an identifiable collaborative workflow.
creativity_rationale: The shared editable HTML canvas plus agent presence, comments, and design-system continuity is a fresh and memorable interaction model for agent-assisted design.
creativity_evidence: Every layer is real HTML rather than an image-only generation result.
Agent appears as a collaborator that can ask permission before pinning notes.
One source canvas is used to derive multiple brand applications.
usability_note: The demonstrated workflow is understandable and preserves human control, though the editor is visually dense.
advance_reason: High leverage and unusually clear product-motion evidence for a genuinely collaborative design workflow.

one_line: A control plane that routes local AI plans through execution lanes with proof and approval boundaries.
what_it_does: InnerOS Mission Control lets a user converse with a local copilot, select an execution lane, approve a refined plan, dispatch it, and inspect delivery evidence.
leverage_rationale: The proposed value is structured routing, governed execution, and verifiable backend hops rather than clicking a generic UI; WebMCP is central to the control-plane surface, though no video means operation is less directly proven.
leverage_evidence: Pitch explicitly describes WebMCP coding control plane and real agent lanes.
About text specifies approval as the execution boundary and selected-lane dispatch.
Frames show staged ask/route/execute/proof interface and trace-oriented panels.
execution_rationale: The screenshots show a substantial, coherent cockpit and the written workflow is detailed, but there is no submitted video or end-to-end result evidence, so execution is capped.
execution_evidence: Demo is marked alive and public repo exists.
Frames show consistent dashboard screens, controls, and proof/trace concepts.
No video transcript or direct completion sequence is provided.
impact_rationale: A governed cockpit for local models, coding agents, infrastructure, and physical automation addresses a real operator need where auditability and explicit approval matter.
impact_evidence: About text names coding, operations, infrastructure, and physical automation workflows.
Approval boundary and verifiable proof are clearly articulated.
Visible interface is organized around execution and evidence rather than chat alone.
creativity_rationale: Combining local AI deliberation, multiple executor lanes, WebMCP routing, and evidence traces is ambitious and more than a generic chat wrapper.
creativity_evidence: Distinct ask-route-execute-watch-proof interaction model.
Backend-hop verification and lane selection are integrated into the product concept.
Frames show a mission-control presentation rather than a simple tool call.
usability_note: The cockpit communicates a clear sequence, but many controls and small labels appear dense.
red_flags: No submitted video or transcript; end-to-end claims are primarily textual.
advance_reason: High-impact agent-infrastructure concept with credible visible UI, but merits evidence-aware comparison against stronger end-to-end demos.

one_line: An agent-accessible kitchen inventory, recipe, and grocery manager.
what_it_does: PantryOS tracks ingredients, quantities, expiry, recipes, serving sizes, and shopping needs, allowing an agent to plan meals and update kitchen state.
leverage_rationale: Structured access to inventory, expiry, recipes, and grocery state can remove substantial manual cross-referencing, though the same tasks remain possible through UI automation with friction.
leverage_evidence: About text lists structured tools for inventory inspection, expiry evaluation, recipe retrieval, quantity updates, and grocery planning.
Use case combines expiring ingredients with recipe and shopping-list updates.
No frame sheet was submitted, so tool behavior is not visually verified.
execution_rationale: The project description is coherent and the demo is alive, but the only image is a Devpost page whose embedded demo is blocked; core workflow completion is not evidenced.
execution_evidence: Public repo and live demo are reported.
About text describes a complete kitchen-management domain model.
Screenshot shows blocked media and no product UI.
impact_rationale: Home cooks have a clear recurring problem in coordinating inventory, expiry, recipes, and shopping, and the proposed combined workflow directly addresses it.
impact_evidence: Description identifies separated kitchen information as the problem.
Concrete four-person expiring-food recipe-and-shopping scenario is given.
Capabilities cover fridge, freezer, pantry, and grocery planning.
creativity_rationale: The unified kitchen state and agent action loop are a useful new angle on a familiar meal-planning category, but the concept is not highly novel.
creativity_evidence: Homogenizes inventory, recipes, expiry, and groceries for agent access.
Agent updates persistent kitchen state rather than only recommending meals.
usability_note: The described workflow is practical, but the interface and actual flow cannot be assessed from the blocked screenshot.
red_flags: Embedded demonstration is blocked by a connection-security error.
advance_reason: Good problem fit, but execution and WebMCP evidence are too thin for advancement in this packet.

one_line: A policy-controlled marketplace where agents negotiate deals while owners retain approval.
what_it_does: ClawDeals lets an agent search, compare, ask sellers questions, and prepare offers under budget and privacy constraints, with server-side policy checks and redacted receipts.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP provides structured, page-scoped negotiation capabilities and shared policy/approval state across an inherently asynchronous marketplace; generic UI driving cannot comparably guarantee constraints, bilateral consent, and receipts.
leverage_evidence: Frames show an e-bike mission with target price, hard cap, radius, battery requirement, seller questioning, and approval pause.
About text describes server-side re-checks of budgets, consent, reservations, and contact reveal.
Devpost screenshot shows live compatibility and 11 registered tools.
execution_rationale: The storyboard presents a coherent search-to-negotiation-to-owner-approval flow with refusal/escalation behavior; no video lowers certainty about actual runtime completion.
execution_evidence: Frames show in-budget offer preparation stopping for confirmation and over-cap escalation.
Frames show untrusted seller data handling and policy checks.
Devpost screenshot presents live demo controls and tool registry.
impact_rationale: Peer-to-peer buyers need negotiation, budget enforcement, and privacy protection, and the demonstrated solution directly addresses high-risk delegated commerce.
impact_evidence: Concrete used-e-bike scenario includes price, location, and battery constraints.
Product targets used goods, furniture, electronics, housing, and similar negotiated markets.
Manual bilateral contact reveal and redacted receipts address real trust concerns.
creativity_rationale: The combination of buyer/seller agents, explicit owner policy, negotiation threads, bilateral consent, and auditable receipts is a memorable and ambitious interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Human plus agent marketplace is more than catalog search or cart automation.
Mechanical-claw metaphor is carried into trust and policy design.
Agent stops at sensitive boundaries rather than pretending to replace consent.
usability_note: The mission and approval states are legible, with clear owner control; marketplace complexity remains substantial.
advance_reason: One of the strongest packets: transformative structured-agent delta, credible workflow evidence, and high real-world value.

one_line: A lecture desk where an agent can seek, highlight, draw, and answer questions in sync with playback.
what_it_does: Classmate combines video, captions, notes, a board, and a ChatGPT sidebar around one lecture clock, with agent actions applied directly to the learning workspace.
leverage_rationale: The agent's ability to act on synchronized playback state—seeking, highlighting, drawing, and generating study artifacts—is meaningfully more precise than narrating screenshots or clicking a generic player UI.
leverage_evidence: Pitch explicitly contrasts page actions with screenshot narration.
About text describes one LectureEngine clock synchronizing video, transcript, slides, notes, and board.
No frame sheet was submitted and the Devpost video is private, limiting verification.
execution_rationale: The described product is coherent, but the inaccessible private video and absent frame sheets leave the central workflow unobserved.
execution_evidence: Live URL and public repo are reported.
About text gives detailed interaction semantics and fallback behavior.
Screenshot visibly shows only a private-video placeholder, not the running product.
impact_rationale: Students have a clear need for contextual lecture questions, synchronized notes, highlights, and flashcards; the product targets that need directly.
impact_evidence: Description gives lecture study use case and timestamped questions.
Features include captions, notes, board, upload, and flashcard generation.
Agent writes on the same study desk rather than only answering externally.
creativity_rationale: Treating the webpage as a shared lecture desk and giving the agent temporal, visual, and board actions is a fresh educational interaction model.
creativity_evidence: One clock synchronizes multiple learning surfaces.
Ask/Lost/Got it controls remain on-page and tied to lecture moments.
Agent operates the desk rather than merely describing content.
usability_note: The interaction model sounds approachable, but actual UI usability cannot be checked because the demo is private.
advance_reason: Promising concept and leverage, but packet evidence is insufficient for a confident execution judgment.

one_line: An AI-hosted playground for Vietnamese folk games and cultural storytelling.
what_it_does: Sân Chơi hosts five Vietnamese folk games with deterministic rules, 3D/animated scenes, procedural audio, persistence, and a broad WebMCP tool surface for an agent game master.
leverage_rationale: The agent is not just explaining games; it manages boards, dice, puppet-show directions, chants, and state-shaped gameplay tools, which is substantially more reliable than UI imitation for a game master.
leverage_evidence: About text describes rules.ts logic called directly by agent tools and JSON state returns.
Project claims 32 registered tools and a debug fallback.
Frame sheets show the game landing/card presentation, but not detailed gameplay state.
execution_rationale: The architecture and product scope are unusually specific, and frames show a coherent polished entry experience; the submitted visual evidence does not demonstrate a full game end to end.
execution_evidence: About text identifies five games, deterministic rules, Three.js/GSAP scenes, audio, and local persistence.
Devpost screenshot shows a playable Sân Chơi demo entry screen.
Frame sheets show repeated branded game cards and calls to play.
impact_rationale: The project serves children and families interested in Vietnamese cultural play, with credible preservation, language, and entertainment value.
impact_evidence: Description identifies vanishing folk traditions and a child-focused motivation.
Five named culturally specific games and puppet theatre are included.
Vietnamese AI game-master framing supports participation rather than passive content.
creativity_rationale: An AI game master for a culturally grounded set of folk games, combining deterministic rules, 3D water puppetry, and synthesized traditional instruments, is highly original and ambitious.
creativity_evidence: Five distinct folk experiences share a common agent-hosted playground.
Three.js water-puppet stage and procedural đàn bầu/percussion deepen the concept.
Cultural authenticity is treated as a core interaction requirement.
usability_note: The entry experience is clear and playful; the breadth of five games may create navigation complexity.
red_flags: No video transcript; frame sheets show entry/card states more than complete play.
advance_reason: Distinctive concept with strong ambition, credible architecture, and meaningful cultural impact.

one_line: A collaborative map that helps an agent decompose complex ideas into questions, insights, and experiments.
what_it_does: Thinking Map stores a goal and source documents as a visual map, then lets an agent gather information and draft connected insights and experiments.
leverage_rationale: Structured map nodes and attached source context can make agent collaboration more persistent and inspectable than a chat, but the same decomposition is possible with general-purpose agent interaction at real but not extreme friction.
leverage_evidence: About text describes goal, attached files, source documents, idea cards, insights, and experiments.
Screenshot visibly shows a prompt card and AI-guidance interface.
No frame sheets and video appears as a packaging preview rather than observed interaction.
execution_rationale: The concept and screenshot are coherent, but the packet does not demonstrate the full map-building workflow or end-state outputs.
execution_evidence: Devpost screenshot visibly shows the prompt and input workflow.
About text describes a twenty-page source and map progression.
No direct end-to-end product motion is available.
impact_rationale: People planning software or researching complex problems can benefit from externalizing unknowns and experiments, though the audience/problem fit is broader and less sharply evidenced than specialized tools.
impact_evidence: Description targets complex problem solving and application planning.
Inspiration cites difficulty communicating desired software behavior.
Source documents and structured questions support concrete planning work.
creativity_rationale: A persistent visual map of what an idea needs to know, with agent-generated research and experiments, is a fresh synthesis beyond ordinary chat brainstorming.
creativity_evidence: Idea is a central node with hanging knowledge questions.
Insights and experiments are drafted as information is gathered.
Whole source documents are retained as map context.
usability_note: The opening question and map metaphor are approachable, but the packet does not show navigation through a completed map.
red_flags: Evidence is primarily Devpost copy and a single packaging screenshot.
advance_reason: Interesting product direction, but limited evidence prevents confident execution and leverage scoring above the middle range.

one_line: A no-sign-up invoice generator whose marketing site is itself an agent-operable capability surface.
what_it_does: Every publishes WebMCP tools for live product/pricing explanation and for creating, updating, converting, and retrieving invoices or proposals, including a viewable result.
leverage_rationale: The agent can discover and execute a real invoice workflow from a marketing page without login, with structured tools spanning decision and creation; generic browsing would be less reliable, though invoice forms are familiar.
leverage_evidence: About text lists 17 tools covering fit/pricing, invoice creation, updates, conversion, PDFs, and retrieval.
Frames show create_invoice implementation, invoice dashboard, and no-sign-up messaging.
Demo narrative includes agent correcting stale search knowledge from live page capabilities.
execution_rationale: Screenshots show a concrete invoice UI, tool implementation, and management/dashboard states, but no frame conclusively shows a newly created invoice end to end.
execution_evidence: Frame sheets show user-facing generator, create_invoice code, persisted invoice fields, and dashboard.
Devpost screenshot visibly identifies the no-sign-up invoice product.
No video transcript and result completion is not directly shown.
impact_rationale: Small service businesses and occasional invoice senders have a specific need for fast invoice creation without account friction; the product directly addresses it.
impact_evidence: No-sign-up invoice generation is explicit.
Tools cover creation through document retrieval/PDF workflow.
Target audience is small service businesses and visitors arriving from search.
creativity_rationale: Making a marketing site an agent-operable, self-describing capability surface and using it to correct stale search knowledge is a sharp, memorable WebMCP application.
creativity_evidence: Product turns live page capability into the answer to outdated search summaries.
Agent-first no-account flow is integrated into the generator rather than bolted onto chat.
17 tools cover the full visitor journey.
usability_note: No-sign-up and structured actions reduce friction, while invoice workflows remain familiar.
red_flags: The frame montage shows implementation and UI but not an unmistakable completed invoice result.
advance_reason: Strong, specific WebMCP leverage with tangible business utility and unusually thoughtful live-page capability story.

one_line: A synthetic security proving ground that makes agent actions auditable and human-approved.
what_it_does: DungeonQ admits bounded scenario packs, simulates decisions, requests human review, applies only approved synthetic effects, verifies receipts, compensates them, and exports replayable evidence.
leverage_rationale: The product depends on structured, state-shaped tools and a deliberate absence of an approval tool: WebMCP enables deterministic scenario state, progressive capability contraction, receipts, and shared human/agent authority that UI driving cannot reproduce reliably.
leverage_evidence: About text enumerates admit/status/simulate/approval-request/effect/receipt/rollback/evidence tools.
Frames show proposal/request/human-approval/proof stages and explicit NO APPROVAL TOOL.
Frames visibly show scenario invalidation, session unchanged, attestation, correlation, and deny states.
execution_rationale: The storyboard visibly demonstrates bounded scenarios, adversarial rejection, preserved session evidence, and human approval/proof states; the absence of a transcript means some claims remain packaging-level.
execution_evidence: Frames show SCENARIO_INVALID and SESSION UNCHANGED after bad input.
Frames show evidence-bound proposal, human UI, deny, and canonical digest concepts.
Devpost screenshot identifies a concrete security proving-ground demo.
impact_rationale: Agentic security and operations need a safe, testable boundary between proposal and approval; this gives evaluators a credible synthetic environment for testing that boundary.
impact_evidence: About text targets adaptive cyber defense and dangerous high-impact autonomous changes.
Three fixed-seed scenarios and judge-authored packs support repeatable evaluation.
Receipt, compensation, and replayable evidence address audit and recovery needs.
creativity_rationale: The concept makes approval absence, progressive tool contraction, synthetic effects, compensation, and evidence replay first-class product mechanics—an ambitious and memorable security interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Agent requests review and then stops; human UI is the authority.
No approval tool and canonical digest/revision prevent hidden override.
Adversarial packs, deny decisions, rollback, and proof form a cohesive proving ground.
usability_note: The staged evidence flow is clear for technical evaluators, though the security vocabulary and dense dashboard may challenge general users.
advance_reason: Outstanding leverage and strong evidence for a serious, original security proving ground.

one_line: Real Santiago restaurant and art-store pages expose catalog, stock, and reservation actions to agents while stopping before commitment.
what_it_does: Tengu and Boykot publish live menu/catalog/search/stock/cart and reservation-form tools; the agent gathers details and fills forms but the human sends or pays.
leverage_rationale: Page-scoped tools turn messy real-business menus, catalogs, stock, and forms into reliable agent actions while preserving a human commitment boundary; generic browsing struggles especially with PDFs, iframes, and live stock.
leverage_evidence: About text lists five Tengu tools and thirteen Boykot tools, including live menu, search, stock, cart, and reservation preparation.
Pitch explicitly says agent does tedious part and stops before send/pay.
Frames show real restaurant branding, menu/reservation content, and reservation form states.
execution_rationale: The packet presents two real-business surfaces with coherent branded pages and concrete tool descriptions, but no video transcript or direct successful agent run is supplied.
execution_evidence: Live demo and public repo are reported.
Frame sheets show Tengu restaurant and bar/reservation pages with forms and calls to action.
Devpost screenshot confirms the project and real-business framing.
impact_rationale: Restaurants and small shops have a real discoverability and booking/cart problem, and consumers benefit when agents can perform preparation without unsafe final commitment.
impact_evidence: About text identifies stale menus and inaccessible booking widgets as the problem.
Two concrete businesses demonstrate restaurant and art-supply use cases.
Human send/pay boundary is aligned with sensitive real-world transactions.
creativity_rationale: Applying WebMCP to real independent businesses and deliberately designing a stop-before-commit pattern is a strong, grounded interaction concept.
creativity_evidence: One pattern spans a fine-dining restaurant and a 3,000-SKU art store.
Tools make businesses authors of current agent-visible truth.
Reservation preparation stops short of autonomous booking/payment.
usability_note: The familiar menu/catalog and reservation surfaces plus explicit stopping point should be approachable.
red_flags: No transcript; frame sheets show site and forms more clearly than actual agent invocation.
advance_reason: Strong practical WebMCP use case with credible live-business context and a well-chosen safety boundary.
